cause_assessments.reason: The original native river.submit box is fully visible and the approved side strip is inside its flat rounded-button fill, clear of glyphs, borders and the host. Frozen sampling consistently measures a changed disabled face, and the original PNG visibly shows the same dimming across the button. The source uses PlainButtonStyle with disabled(selected == nil); the palette value exists in source but the disabled style changes the final rendered face. The policy assigns primary fill to the component. This is a component disabled-appearance defect, not host/canvas sampling or infrastructure. The exact opacity/compositing mechanism is inferred; the ownership and rendered-fill contradiction are directly supported.

Original state-scoped PNGs show the disabled primary control fully inside the actual viewport. Its approved side strip is a uniform interior fill, clear of label glyphs and corners, and the frozen sampler confirms full solid-color support. The sampled region belongs to the component primary button, not the outer host. Source uses PlainButtonStyle with .disabled and the intended palette background, while the actual disabled appearance is altered; source palette declarations do not override original rendered pixels. The component owns the final opaque action fill, so this is a product appearance defect (disabled-style compositing), not a mapping/environment or unsuitable-observation failure.

cause_assessments.reason: The original native river.submit box is fully visible and the approved side strip is inside its flat rounded-button fill, clear of glyphs, borders and the host. Frozen sampling consistently measures a changed disabled face, and the original PNG visibly shows the same dimming across the button. The source uses PlainButtonStyle with disabled(selected == nil); the palette value exists in source but the disabled style changes the final rendered face. The policy assigns primary fill to the component. This is a component disabled-appearance defect, not host/canvas sampling or infrastructure. The exact opacity/compositing mechanism is inferred; the ownership and rendered-fill contradiction are directly supported.

Original state-scoped PNGs show the disabled primary control fully inside the actual viewport. Its approved side strip is a uniform interior fill, clear of label glyphs and corners, and the frozen sampler confirms full solid-color support. The sampled region belongs to the component primary button, not the outer host. Source uses PlainButtonStyle with .disabled and the intended palette background, while the actual disabled appearance is altered; source palette declarations do not override original rendered pixels. The component owns the final opaque action fill, so this is a product appearance defect (disabled-style compositing), not a mapping/environment or unsuitable-observation failure.

judge_two.reason: Direct original own-D0 support in the exact P2/ios/replaced state: inspected every cited original PNG and its native river.submit control/semantic box (snapshots [151, 152, 153]); it is disabled, unique and fully visible. clusters_one.reason: All four confirmed product rows are the disabled primary control in P1/P2 baseline/replaced. Independent inspection of the common original D0 frames confirms the same state-dependent altered primary face. The one D0 SwiftUI component constructs that primary with the intended palette fill followed by PlainButtonStyle and .disabled(selected == nil). Baseline and authoritative replacement both leave no valid selection, reaching this same disabled path; P1/P2 only select light/dark palette values. Original own samples reproduce the corresponding uniform light/dark deviations. The source and repeated appearance support one shared disabled-rendering cause, not four independent bugs. The exact framework opacity/compositing formula is inferred, while common path, ownership, and membership are directly supported. Android has no confirmed product row.

clusters_two.reason: All four manifestations use the same original SwiftUI RiverSensorTriageBoard.swift primary-button implementation and no-selection disabled path: the action label receives palette.disabled as its background inside Button, then PlainButtonStyle and .disabled(selected == nil) apply. The same source is used for P1/P2; only the theme palette and text scale differ. Own-D0 and common-D0 original native boxes and all cited screenshots show the same altered fill in baseline and replaced within each theme (#FFCFCDC5 for light instead of #FFAAA99F, #FF33474C for dark instead of #FF52666A). Approved ownership assigns the final solid primary face to the component. Repeated states and theme variants are manifestations of the shared disabled-action appearance path, not four independent bugs. The precise framework opacity/compositing internals remain inferred, but the shared source path, state trigger and rendered contradiction establish this cause membership. No Android or unconfirmed wrapping rows are included.
